item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Here, for example, I maintain that it is totally unnecessary, you easily could have given the same conclusion through observations of these entities and what happens if the glamour gland is damaged or removes, IMO.

See, one of the meta things that appeal to me about the Foundation is that we are dealing with the implied supernatural through thoroughly mundane means. Finding the science (or better said, regularities and laws governing) in an anomaly through experimentation is cool. Hey, occassional use of an SCP to contain something else is also cool, because of the implications - we don't quite understand how it works, but it's our best bet in the situation.

Having a generic, completely technobabbley explanation for everything like the Humes are is something I'd expect in the sourcebook of d20 Modern (or another urban fantasy RPG) as an acceptable, if a little cheap way to implement a magic system. Here it strikes me as something that outright devalues a lot of the content we have.

item.content:encoded:
hard and expensive to build and maintain

Kant Meters seem to require that SRAs are easy and cheap enough to build that you can miniaturize them and put two of them into a handheld device. They have to be pretty trivial to maintain too, or you wouldn't be using a handheld instrument at all and measuring Humes would be a tricky business done only in the lab with a lot of inherent unreliability due to finicky equipment.

not to mention that you're having to drain the very reality from dead universes

That would seem to be an infinite resource.

they can't just be used willy-nilly to neutralize anomalies.

But can be used willy-nilly to measure Humes?

I think it it runs the risk of being lazy technobabble that doesn't even look too hard at its own implications. Here, for example, I maintain that it is totally unnecessary, you easily could have given the same conclusion through observations of these entities and what happens if the glamour gland is damaged or removed, IMO.

item.content:encoded:
Well written but extremely boring. It's just an alternate human history with elves/fairies/whatever in it, and that timeline seems to have just gone pretty much like how our own history did, which seems kinda implausible (and also the most boring outcome to read). Human history has been hugely influenced by technological and scientific discoveries, and having a society in Europe that's straight up capable of magic would have changed everything, pretty much from day one.

Writing an entire world history is a huge endeavor and the article doesn't really need it either. A bunch of interviews and recorded encounters and artifacts that the Foundation has compiled would be a much more interesting way to provide insight into Fairy world history, and also allow you to be a lot more vague and suggest at a more complicated, distinctive and interesting world that you won't actually have to write the entire history of.
